title: Why does this chapter begin with seeing and end with being seen?

beats.narration: This chapter opens with 'have you seen?' and ends with people praying just to be seen. Coincidence?
The closing verses describe people who pray while inattentive — those who put themselves on display. The verb is yura'un: not seeing, but getting yourself seen, performed for an audience.
Now hear the chapter's very first word: a-ra'ayta — have you seen? Same root. The surah opens by summoning your sight, and closes on people who only crave to be a sight.
Two gazes, set against each other: seeing that discloses what is true, and performing to be seen. Between them stand an orphan unhelped and a prayer gone hollow.
